# A flow of rich text, parsed by a real browser.
#
# The golden in testdata/markup_inline.txtar shows the markup html writes. What
# it cannot show is what a browser makes of it, and the family's two claims
# about text are claims about exactly that: the characters an author wrote are
# text and not markup, and every one of them survives.
#
# So this snapshots `document.documentElement.outerHTML` after the page has
# loaded -- the DOM as Chromium parsed it, not the bytes that were served.
#
# `<em>not markup</em>` is the assertion in the first form. Written into a
# `markup.text`, it must come back as four escaped entities inside the one
# span; if the escaping were dropped anywhere between the emitter and the page,
# the browser would have built an `<em>` element and the DOM would say so. The
# only element in this document is the `<strong>` that `markup.bold` is.
#
# Two spaces and a newline are the assertion in the second. A text node holds
# what it holds whatever the CSS says, so the two spaces and the line break
# below prove the characters reached the page; `white-space: pre-wrap` in the
# live DOM is what makes the browser render them rather than collapse them.
# That last step is layout and is not asserted here -- what is asserted is that
# the declaration survived onto the element the flow rendered as.
#
# Confirmed by reverting: with `html.EscapeString` taken off the static text
# path, `sngl test` still reports PASS and one passing test, and the first grep
# below is what fails. An injection is invisible to a state assertion and shows
# up only in the DOM, which is the whole reason this fixture reads one.


env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
exists app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html

grep '&lt;em&gt;not markup&lt;/em&gt;' app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html
! grep '<em>' app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html
grep '<strong><span> bold</span></strong>' app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html
grep '&gt;  two spaces' app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html
grep '^and a newline' app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html
grep 'white-space:pre-wrap' app.sngl.snapshots/rendered.html

# And the snapshot is stable: a second run compares against what the first
# wrote rather than writing it again.
env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import md "sngl:ui/markup"

output { none { html } }

component main node {
    md.paragraph {
        md.text(value="<em>not markup</em>  two spaces\nand a newline")
        md.bold {
            md.text(value=" bold")
        }
    }
}

func testRendered(t Test, c main) {
    t.snapshot("rendered")
}

window {
    main
}
-- testrun/html/none/app.sngl/main/1 --
